sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Locating the .env files
sections.what: Works out where two possible .env files should sit, one inside the AI service folder and one at the project root.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the service find its settings whether it is started from the service folder or the project root.
sections.watch_out: The paths are computed from this file's location, so moving the file breaks the lookup.

sections.name: Settings
sections.title: Settings and their defaults
sections.what: Defines every setting with a default: environment, log level, Redis and database addresses, Groq and OpenAI keys, models and endpoints, the OpenAI temperature, and the Pinecone key and index. Blank keys mean that provider is not used.
sections.why: Likely reason: defaults let the service start for local development without extra setup.
sections.watch_out: The default database address includes a simple local password that must be changed for any shared or hosted environment.

summary: Loads all AI service settings from environment variables and .env files into one settings object.
purpose: Gives the rest of the AI service one place to read API keys, model names, and addresses.
why: Likely reason: keeps secrets and environment-specific values out of the code. Reason for looking in two .env locations is not stated.
how: First it works out where two possible .env files should be, one in the AI service folder and one at the project root. Then it defines each setting with a default, including the Groq and OpenAI endpoints and models, the OpenAI temperature, and the Pinecone key and index. It reads values from the environment and those files, ignores unknown names, and creates one shared settings object.
outputs: A single settings object used by the chatbot and summarizer.
risks: Defaults include a local database password. Empty API keys silently switch the service to mock or demonstration output. The temperature setting exists but the chatbot does not use it. The default Groq model here differs from the example file.
debug: If the wrong model is used, check the environment variables first. In pydantic-settings, environment variables normally take priority over .env files. If the service returns mock output, check that the key is set and not empty.
